newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Qantas wants genuine airport charges.
newsitem.headline: Qantas wants genuine airport charges.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd called on Monday for the Australian government to ensure clearly justified pricing structures following the sale of Australia's airports.

"Whilst airlines have no problems paying for services which are essential to the processing of passengers and cargo and for maintaining safe aircraft operations, they have long been concerned to ensure that such services are genuinely costed," Qantas' general manager for government and international relations, David Hawes, told an aviation conference.
"If transparency is denied, then trust and confidence wanes," Hawes said.
"This accounts for a degree of tension in the relationship between the airlines and the FAC (Federal Airports Corp) -- tension which the new airport operators seem likely to inherit."
The government has 10 consortiums short-listed as bidders in the first phase of airport privatisation, the sale of 50-year leases for Brisbane, Perth and Melbourne airports.
Hawes said airlines were also concerned that the definition of aeronautical services did not include a number of directly related operations.
"These included aircraft hangers, jet base facilities, overhaul shops and the like," he said.
He said previous attempts to have these services included within the definition had been unsuccessful.
"The issue is important because the smaller the ambit, the greater will be the opportunity for airports to extract monopoly rents unchecked," he said.
Hawes said the transition to private airport ownership had also thrown up uncertainties about infrastructure regulation.
"These uncertainties could affect efficiency and cost in airline terminal expansion and airline ground operations," he said.
